you rely on non-standard controller setups

cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: New players encounter controller issues, missing auto-reload, and broken remote co-op.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that controller support fails or breaks during gameplay when using non-Xbox controllers or Steam input translation layers.

citations.review_text: seems to be a nice game but it completely f***ed up controller support.

I hate to leave a bad review based on controller support alone, but it is a twin stick shooter. This is one of few PC games I would prefer to play on controller, and that is the whole reason I bought the game. From what I can tell, this game only natively supports Xbox controllers. My old Xbox One controller went to the big RRoD in the sky, so I borrowed a controller from my dusty PS4 Pro. Steam's controller translation layer thingy worked great.. for 15 minutes, then forced the sticks to run me into a corner and no buttons would work except start, or whatever Sony calls that button, and the d-pad. Maybe it was a fluke, or there's an easy workaround. If so, i'll change my reccomendation. I still think it's a big oversight for a twin-stick shooter to not support a controller as common as the DualShock, even if it is inferior to Xbox controllers. I can't rightly recommend a game where you can't even make it to the 3rd floor unless you only use a controller made by Microsoft.

edit: yeah... thought it would be safe to save before 2nd floor in case something went wrong. Launch came, continue, sticks don't work thanks to Steam's busted controller input thing. I'm assuming the save is deleted as soon as loaded, which makes sense for a roguelite, to prevent savescumming, but sucks for a game where the controls break every 10 - 15 minutes if you're using Steam input. Would probably be a great game on Xbox controller or even M+KB, otherwise unplayable unless you prefer playing the first floor over and over.

claims.claim: Reviewers note the absence of an auto-reload feature when holding down the shoot button.

citations.review_text: No option to auto-reload when holding down the shoot button.

Pretty disappointed in this one although it's only been an hour. The movement (especially dodge rolls) and shooting are both really awkward, slow, and unsatisfying. The reloading mechanic is just not fun as it happens way too often and takes way too long. The UI is poorly made with crappy presentation of information. I do NOT recommend using a controller. At least not one without a touchpad like a steam controller.

It goes from boring to bullet hell in a split second when you get to a boss. So you do ten minutes of boring exploration in a dull environment not getting hit by anything and then die in 3 seconds when you get to a boss when a bunch of expanding bullet spirals come out of nowhere. And I like expanding bullet spirals that come out of nowhere. But it's not fun dodging when the movement is so slow and awkward. I like difficult games, but this isn't difficult in a fun way. It doesn't seem like getting better at it is going to actually be fun, because the game play itself is generally just not fun or satisfying.

In a good bullet hell game the movement and the enemies/bullets are matched in a way that makes the game flow and keeps you at the edge of what you can handle as the intensity builds through a level, and when you get to the boss you're prepared for it. There's no flow in this game. You just walk around until you find the boss room and hope you got lucky enough with the gear you found that it's not just 30 seconds of stupidity followed by a restart.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the cooperative multiplayer as broken or difficult to set up properly for remote play.

citations.review_text: Got catfished. Thought it was online coop. Found out it can only be done by doing play together and its borked. Person playing remotely controller couldn't move the coop player.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as running very well on low-end hardware or older systems.

citations.review_text: Still fun to play even after all these years. Great variety of guns and items. The synergy system makes you want to grind for new items. Replayability is practically infinite. Runs well even on a literal potato.

As much as I waned to like this game, in the end it failed to shine.

I am very sorry to write this negative review as I have given the game several attempts in over 2 hours with every possible approach just so as to dig up an excuse to push it into "Recommend", as the potential was immense.

Pros:
The design is cute and well optimized to be fast, without unnecessary loading times.
The idea of being a quick-paced bullet hell was well technically prepared and there were no bugs, slow responses, or glitches.

Cons:

The greatest irony is that the game based its main mechanic around strategy-shifting inventiveness based on an expected myriad of different-shooting weapons - which turned out to be a total miss (!pun intended).

Not only is a vast majority of weapons useless in terms of damage dealt to bosses with no more difference than in cosmetic quirks, but also do new weapons come up so rarely that in most of runs I ended up having the starting weak weapon as the only one up to the level boss.

As the main difference from "Binding of Isaac", for example, that has its own webpages dedicated to the complexity of not only how weapons and items interact with each other, but also that actually gives you palpable progress as you move on, "Enter the Gungeon" is so absolutely random that it keeps you in the shallows unless by some immense stroke of luck in one in 10 runs you happen to find a weapon worth having - and by that the single measuring point are the bosses - the game has unlockable characters and items that supposedly shift this, but gives no drive to invest the time to do so.

! - Possible Redeeming Caveat:
Some characters that happen along the way can unlock new weapons and behaviors, but honestly the game provided very little incentive to invest in multiple runs while relying on pure luck.

Except for bosses and a slight few regular enemies, the enemies didn't pose a challenge.
But the bosses weren't even that difficult as much as they were s…

The game starts out pretty tough (though that could just be me since I'm new to PC gaming and using a keyboard and mouse), but the more you play, the more addictive it gets. Finding new guns and fighting new enemies and bosses keeps it fun, and since the rooms and chambers are randomized, every run feels new. You have to be careful and strategic because the game is very punishing--if you die, it's game over and you start from scratch. I've always loved games with colorful pixel art, so that's a plus. Another nice thing is that the game is light, so you could probably run it on a potato.

Gotta keep playing bc I still suck at this game....

cohorts.summary: Adventurers figure out mechanics independently with minimal upfront explanation.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game drops players in with minimal explanation, requiring them to figure out systems on their own.

citations.review_text:
Challenging game for people like challenges. It is more grinding than fun.

Lack of feeling of the progress, like RPG. The progress is achieved by unlock more items you can pickup/find randomly in the game process. The explainations on items are not clear. I had to Google them all the time.

Greatest game I have ever played! If you like games where dodging and skill is key, you will love this. This game drops you into it with very little explanation and you have to figure it out yourself. 10/10 game!

cohorts.summary: Long-term players master challenging bullet-hell combat while noting rare enemy spawns and camera limitations in local co-op.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as a difficult and challenging bullet-hell roguelike, noting that it has a steep learning curve and requires mastering mechanics, enemy patterns, and boss fights.

citations.review_text:
An excellent bullet-hell roguelike. The game is genuinely difficult, especially when first learning its mechanics, enemy patterns and bosses, but the progession is extremely satisfying. The game can become repetitive at time but the satisfaction of getting further and eventually defeating the hardest bosses makes worth it.

100% Completion
Time : 142.7H
Completion Difficulty : 8/10
Playthroughs : Many run
Missables : None
Notable requirements : defeat all bosses, complete numerous challenges.
This game is just chaotic wacky fun; Very difficult though. Completely fair, generally speaking, but very difficult.

Yes. Buy this. Enter the Gungeon is among the best roguelites I've ever seen, and it's what first introduced me to both roguelites and bullet hells. It is a game that I keep coming back to even after seeing it all.

It's got tons of potential items and guns to unlock, many of them whimsical or a reference that you will be giddy about when you get it. This is one of those games that you can feel the love, not just for the game, but for all of nerd and gaming culture.

You will not regret picking this up, although you should know it is incredibly difficult. That's what happens when you get a good roguelite/bullet hell. But it is worth every death just to experience this gem a little more.

Also, while my hours show 156 as of review, bear in mind I have completed this game on both Xbox and Switch before getting it on Steam. That's how good this game is.

P.S. When you do feel like you've seen it all, check out the Thunderstore mod manager. You can mod the game from there to have so much more content.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game lacks built-in online co-op and note that the local co-op camera implementation is poor.

citations.review_text:
Endless unlocks, great gameplay, simple to learn. Absolutely adore this game and cant wait to EtG2.

Only problem: no built in online co-op, local co-op camera sucks.

The game is king in its genre, very rare to find a game of such class these days. Only thing missing is online co-op.

P.S. never conserve ammo, its called bullet hell for a reason.

claims.claim: Reviewers point out that enemy hunt quests have very low spawn rates, making completion take an exceptionally long time.

citations.review_text:
[h1]5/5 Perfectly wacky bullet-hell[/h1]
[h2]For how much content this game offers anything less than 5/5 would be shameful. I just wish there was more synergies with the unique guns but there are limitations when it comes to these things.[/h2]
[h2]Pros:[/h2]
[list]
[*]Tons of wacky weapons. (A shotgun that shoots shotgun shells, Skateboard gun, Unicorn horn, etc)
[*]Synergies for every weapon and passive items.
[*]Secret levels to find and extend your run. (One of them has a mini Punch out game)
[/list]
[h2]Cons:[/h2]
[list]
[*]Bad enemy hunt quest. (Spawn rates are abysmal for some of them taking forever to finish)
[/list]
[h2]Honestly I fail to find that many flaws with the game maybe I'm overlooking more obvious stuff but the game does feel a little bit like The binding of Isaac with it's synergy system, nothing wrong with it but if the game added more synergies then it might become more comparable. But I wouldn't mind this game being the baby's first Isaac game. The game does feel a little short with only 5 levels to go through but the secret levels and clone item does extend that.[/h2]
[h1]In conclusion. [url=https://youtu.be/xZzWiFjsbM0]Enter the gungeon[/url][/h1]

ENNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNter the Gungeon is a pretty dang fun.... theme song!

And a pretty dang fun game too, with lots of clear and obvious strengths! BUT, oh man... there are a LOT of flaws to this game too. Thankfully, I think the game is frontloaded with its strongest elements, so perhaps your first 15 hours of this game might be a near flawless good time! But it's possible to extend this game to like *150* hours like I did, because this game does have a lot to find and achievements to hunt, and that's where I think you'll start noticing the same flaws I did...

Let's start with the positives! I think this game has two MAJOR unique strengths. The first, and my favorite part of this game, is how strongly and consistently it's themed. EVERYTHING IN THIS GAME IS GUN-THEMED! The floors of this dungeon, no, GUNGEON aren't called floors, they're called Chambers! The undead, no, GUNDEAD enemies are sentient bullets and shotgun shells, and the items you pick up tend to be very bullet-themed too. Hah, your "bombs" in this game are called "blanks". You'll find "Ammolets", your bestiary/encyclopedia is called the "Ammonomicon", you might fight a snake enemy called the "Ammoconda", etc etc... it's so fun, so whimsical, and feels like such a simple concept but it leads to so much creative wordplay and designs, that it's really cool to see play out. It's pretty genius!

The second obvious major strength of this game, is the absolutely HUMONGOUS variety of items and weapons to choose from. Even after 100%ing the achievements after 150 hours of playtime, there are still items in the Ammonomicon I have yet to unlock, and weapons I still haven't tried out. In many ways, this creates a ton of replayability: you'll have a long-term objective of discovering new items to fill out your Ammonomicon, but you ALSO get runs that can feel quite different because of the many different weapons and items you can use, some of which even have special combos to discover!
